newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian president approves new PM and government.
newsitem.headline: Estonian president approves new PM and government.

text.p: Estonian President Lennart Meri has approved the new government of Mart Siimann, the president's office said on Sunday.
The new government is barely altered from that of former prime minister Tiit Vaehi, with just two ministers changed, in the agriculture and education portfolios.
Siimann presented his proposed government to Meri on Friday, and the president approved it late on Saturday evening, the president's office said in a statement.
Siimann, 50, replaced Vaehi, a veteran politician who quit last month after 22 months in office.

Vaehi's resignation came after he only narrowly won a no-confidence motion in parliament that was brought amid allegations he was involved in shady privatisation deals involving real estate in central Tallinn.
Siimann, a former television and radio station manager, is the leader of the parliamentary faction of the Coalition Party, one of the two largest groups in parliament.
He was given the authority by parliament on Wednesday to form a new government and had to present his team numbering 15 ministers, including himself, to the president within seven days.
Siimann and the new ministers in the government are expected to take their oaths of office before parliament as soon they can, possibly on Monday.
The new prime minister has already promised to continue the previous government's economic policies and reforms.
He said his government would treat land reform, reforming the pension system and European Union membership as priorities.
Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states with a population of just 1.5 million, is regarded as one of the most successful and committed reformers of the former Soviet republics.
The country has managed to keep on the path of reform despite frequent political turbulence since regaining independence from Moscow in 1991.
